texts.preamble: Subramani M Psi vs Rafeeq Ali on 29 August, 2025 Kabc030900342014 Digitally Deepa signed by Veeraswamy Deepa Veeraswamy Presented on : 26-12-2014 Registered on : 26-12-2014 Decided on : 30-08-2025 Duration : 10 years, 8 months, 4 days In The Court Of The Viii Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City Present: Smt. Deepa.V., B.A.L. Ll B. Viii Acjm, Bengaluru City. Date: this the 29th Day of August, 2025 C.C. No.35854/2021 State by Sanjay Nagara Police Station, Bengaluru. ... Complainant (Represented by Sri. Vishwanath Senior APP) Versus Sri Rafiq Ali, Aged about 52 years, S/o Sri Abdul Samad, R/at No.348, 3rd Main, Basaveshwara Layout, Nagashettihalli, Sanjay Nagar, Bengaluru. ... Accused (Represented By Sri Syed Parvez Ali) KABC030900342014 CC 35854/2021 1.
texts.facts: The Police Sub-Inspector of Sanjay Nagara Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused for the offences punishable under Section 285, 420 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3, 7(1)(a) of Essential Commodities Act and Sec.7, 3(1)(a), 3(b)(c), 6, 4(1)(a) of Gas Supply Act, 2000. 2. Prosecution Case: On 19-10-2021 at House No.348, 3rd Main Road, Basaveshwara Layout, within the limits of Sanjay Nagara Police Station, the accused without obtaining license possessed domestic and commercial gas cylinders of various gas companies unauthorisedly and was refilling to other gas cylinders without adhering to safety measures with an intention to make wrongful gain thereby cheated the Government as well as customers. 3. First Information Report: CW1/PW1 Sri Subramani, PSI of Sanjay Nagara PS, Bengaluru on the receipt of credible information, raided the house bearing No.348, 3rd Main Road, Basaveshwara Layout, Nagashettihalli, Bangalore along with pancha witnesses, staff and found that the accused was refilling the domestic gas to other gas cylinders and hence the accused was taken into custody and conducted spot cum seizure mahazar as per Ex.P1 from 10:20 am to 11:30 am and seized rubber pipe, valve, refilling machine, 3 domestic cylinders of an Indane company, one domestic cylinder of Subramani M Psi vs Rafeeq Ali on 29 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120386314/ 2 Bharat company, two cylinders weighing 5 kg, three cylinders weighing 3 kg, two cylinders weighing 2 kg, weighing machine and produced the same before CW9 and Ex.P2 report was given. The seized properties were handed over to the Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Department by obtaining permission from the court. 4. Investigation: During the course of investigation, on receipt of report from CW1, PW7 Sri Ravhichandra, PSI, registered FIR as per Ex.P2, subjected the properties under PF No.101/2021, recorded the statements of CW2 to CW8, obtained a report from CW6 as per Ex.P4 on seized cylinders, the items seized were handed over to the Food Department, after investigation he filed charge sheet against the accused. 5. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court had taken cognizance of offences alleged against the accused. 6. Copies of prosecution paper as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused. 7. The accused was released on bail at the pre- cognizance stage by the order dated 21-10-2021. 8. Charge: After hearing learned APP and counsel for accused, charge for the offences punishable under Section 285, 420 of IPC and Sec.7 of E.C. Act and Sec.3, 6 and 7 of Gas Supply order, 2000 has been framed, read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 9. Prosecution Evidence: The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 9 witnesses examined all witnesses and exhibited 10 documents and closed their side. The presence of CW2 could not be secured and hence dropped out from examination despite due execution of proclamation by the order dated 11/08/2023. On account of examination of CW7, the examination of CW8 was given up by the order dated 20/08/2025. 10. Accused statement as per section 313 of Cr.P.C: After completion of evidence of prosecution, the accused was examined as per section 313 statement of Cr.P.C wherein he denied all incriminating evidence appearing in the statement of prosecution witnesses and did not lead any rebuttal evidence. 11. In furtherance, rubber pipe, valve, refilling machine, 3 domestic cylinders of an Indian company, one domestic cylinder of a Bharat company, two cylinders weighing 5 kg, three cylinders weighing 3 kg, two cylinders weighing 2 kg, weighing machine were seized and produced before CW9 and Ex.P2 report was given.
texts.arguments: Whenever any place liable to search of inspection under this Chapter is closed, any person residing in, or being in charge of, such place, shall, on demand of the officer or other person executing the warrant, and on production of the warrant, allow him free ingress thereto, and afford all reasonable facilities for a search therein. 2. If ingress into such place cannot be so obtained, the officer or other person executing the warrant may proceed in the manner provided by Sub-Section (2) of section 47. 3. Where any person in or about such place is reasonably suspected of concealing about his person any article for which search should be made, such person may be searched and if such person is a woman, the search shall be made by another woman with strict regard to decency. 4. Before making a search under this Chapter, the officer or other person about to make it shall call upon two or more independent and respectable inhabitants of the locality in which the place to be searched is situate or of any other locality if no such inhabitant of the said locality is available or is willing to be a witness to the search, to attend and witness the search and may issue an order in writing to them or any of them so to do. 5. The search shall be made in their presence, and a list of all things seized in the course of such search and of the places in which they are respectively found shall be prepared by such officer or other person and signed by such witnesses; but no person witnessing a search under this section shall be required to attend the Court as a witness of the search unless specially summoned by it. 6. The occupant of the place searched, or some person in his behalf, shall, in every instance, be permitted to attend during the search, and a copy of the list prepared under this section, signed by the said witnesses, shall be delivered to such occupant or person. 7. When any person is searched under Sub-Section (3), a list of all things taken possession of shall be prepared, and a copy thereof shall be delivered to such person. 8. Any person who, without reasonable cause, refuses or neglects to attend and witness a search under this section, when called upon to do so by an order in writing delivered or tendered to him, shall be deemed to have committed an offence under section 187 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860). It has been held in the case of Pradeep Narayana Vs State of Maharastra reported in AIR 1995 Supreme Court 1930 wherein it was held that failure of police to join witness from locality during search creates doubt Subramani M Psi vs Rafeeq Ali on 29 August, 2025
